goal: A running autopilot daemon publishes a liveness record (PID plus freshness) so a second supervisor reads it, finds the live daemon, and adopts it instead of spawning a duplicate, while a stale record reads as not-live exactly like a lapsed worker lease.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_autopilot_run.py -- the daemon loop (run_daemon_loop, main) is where the liveness record is published/refreshed each cycle

packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_worker_supervisor.py -- has_live_lease() reads task_claims with lease_expires_at > now and treats a past expiry as not-live; mirror this staleness rule exactly for the autopilot record

packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_autopilot_supervisor.py -- today has NO cross-process liveness (the module docstring notes 'autopilot writes no task_claims lease'); this task gives it a record to read so adoption/DETACHED detection becomes possible
constraints: The liveness record's staleness rule MUST match the worker lease-expiry semantics: a record whose freshness is in the past reads as not-live (so a truly dead daemon is respawned, not adopted forever). This is the shared invariant with has_live_lease().
Liveness is read out-of-band from the record's freshness -- never from a status the daemon self-reports (daemon/agent claims are untrusted).
A second supervisor reading a live record must adopt (report DETACHED/adopted) and spawn zero new children; reading a stale record must NOT block respawn.
Prefer reusing an existing store/record surface over adding a new schema table; if a new file/record surface is unavoidable, keep it minimal and document the freshness field.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not add auto-respawn logic here -- that is the console-supervisor and headless-entrypoint tasks; this task ships the liveness record and its read/adopt path plus tests.
Do not modify or weaken existing autopilot-daemon or supervisor tests.
Do not change the worker's task_claims schema or protocol.
Do not touch flywheel_core purity boundaries.
edge_cases: Stale record (freshness in the past) must read as not-live -- this is the case that prevents 'adopt a corpse forever'.
A record from a different daemon pid than the one a supervisor owns must not be mistaken for the owned child (mirror the existing activity-pid guard).
No record at all (fresh project, daemon never ran) reads as not-live, same as a missing lease.
